seen_animation: Frames 1-4: a horse head drawn in black lines faces the viewer, two pointed ears at the top, two small scribbled eyes, a long closed oval face reaching the bottom edge, a zigzag mane line running left along the top, and a thin straight line running from the left edge into the cheek; grey vertical post shapes behind. Frames 5-8: the head is now in profile facing right, the eye on the left side of the face, a jaw corner with a short horizontal chin line, and the muzzle angled down and to the right ending in a flat blunt tip near the bottom right; the mane line stays across the top. Frames 9-10: the profile head drops lower and the muzzle tip moves left and down. Frames 11-12: the head swings back toward a front view, the muzzle narrows and points straight down, and grey zigzag grass appears along the bottom. Frames 13-16: the head is front-facing and low, narrow muzzle near the grass, ears bunched at the top right, the head shifting slightly right and up from 13 to 14 and then holding through 16.
seen_film: Frames 1-2: a pale horse with a long mane faces the camera at a log fence, head filling the center-left. Frames 3-4: the head begins turning to the viewer's right. Frames 5-8: the head is in three-quarter profile facing right, muzzle lowering and moving to the right side of the frame by frame 8. Frames 9-11: the head drops further and comes down and slightly left, muzzle near the bottom of the frame, with hay appearing at the bottom right. Frames 12-16: the head is lowered into a pile of hay at the bottom center-left, nose down, eating, the head nearly front-on to the camera with the ears forward; the head moves slightly between frames while feeding.
named_subject: a horse's head and neck (mane, two ears, one or two eyes, muzzle)
evidence: The overall event matches: front-facing in 1-4 (film 1-4), turn to right profile with muzzle down-right in 5-8 (film 5-8), lowering in 9-12 (film 9-12), head down near the ground in 13-16 (film 13-16). But frame 4 to 5 changes from a closed front oval with two eyes to an open profile with a separate jaw line in one step, and the face outline is redrawn rather than rotated; frame 10 to 11 switches from a right-pointing profile muzzle to a downward front muzzle in one step while the film turns gradually across 9-12; frames 12-13 show the cheek curve on the left drawn as a separate overlapping contour beside the muzzle outline, so the head reads as two shapes; frame 13 to 14 the head jumps right and the ear strokes at the top become a tangle of crossing lines. The film has hay as a mound; the animation shows generic grass spikes, and the head in 14-16 hovers above them rather than pushing into them.
primary_gap: The head changes between front view and profile in single-frame swaps (4 to 5 and 10 to 11) with the outline redrawn, instead of turning through intermediate angles as the film does.
closes_when: Frames 3-5 and 10-12 show the same face outline progressively rotating (eye sliding across the face, near cheek line growing, muzzle tip moving smoothly), with no frame where the contour is replaced by a different construction.
protect: The timing that matches the film (front 1-4, profile 5-8, lowering 9-12, grazing 13-16); the doodle's few-stroke construction, scribbled eye, pointed leaf-shaped ears, zigzag mane line and jaw/chin stroke; the grey scenery staying subordinate to the black character.
identity_gap: The profile frames 5-10 read as the doodle's construction (scribble eye, leaf ears, jaw hook, zigzag mane) mirrored to face right, but the front-view frames 1-4 and 13-16 use a long oval face that the doodle never draws, and the ears in 13-16 become crossed tangled strokes unlike the doodle's two clean ear loops.
